statement: At a tax deed sale on a county-held certificate, the opening bid is the sum of all outstanding certificates on the property plus omitted years' taxes, delinquent taxes, current taxes if due, interest, and all costs and fees paid by the county. On homestead property it also includes one-half of the latest assessed value.
evidence: 2026 Florida Statutes read from the Legislature's site through a read-only capture on 2026-10-05; quoted in docs/available-amount-semantics.md section 2

statement: Property on the county's list of lands available for taxes may, after 90 days, be purchased from the clerk by anyone for the opening bid; interest on the opening bid continues to accrue through the month of sale.
evidence: 2026 Florida Statutes read from the Legislature's site through a read-only capture on 2026-10-05; quoted in docs/available-amount-semantics.md section 2

statement: The purchaser pays the documentary stamp tax and the recording fees, and delinquent taxes or certificates that arose after the tax deed application must be paid.
evidence: 2026 Florida Statutes read from the Legislature's site through a read-only capture on 2026-10-05; quoted in docs/available-amount-semantics.md section 2

statement: Whether and when unsold Lands Available property escheats to the county is cited in this repository (F.S. 197.502(8)) but that subsection's text has not been read and recorded.
How long a tax certificate stays valid is cited in this repository (F.S. 197.482) but the section has not been read and recorded.
Florida's rules for redeeming a certificate before a tax deed is issued have not been read and recorded here.

County tax deed sale calendars and published results are read from each county's RealAuction site. Closed and canceled items are served to the same anonymous session as the upcoming list; a result is shown only through a published wording mapped in data/auction_outcome_wordings.csv.
source_title: RealAuction county tax deed sites (Alachua shown; one site per county)

statement: Bidder registration, deposit and payment deadlines are set per county and per auction site. They are not recorded statewide; see each county's verified procedure below when one exists.

Texas Tax Code section 34.21 governs redemption after a tax sale (this app's Texas copy summarises 180 days, or 2 years for homestead / agricultural property). The statute's text has not been read and recorded here, and the summary is flagged for counsel review (docs/legal/pre-sale-counsel-review.md).

Texas tax foreclosure sales and resales of struck-off property are conducted county by county (in Galveston by the Sheriff). The statewide statutory model (Tex. Tax Code chapter 34) has not been read and recorded here.

Texas listings come from the delinquent-tax counsel's sale site (LGBS) and RealAuction county sheriff-sale sites. They are read only by a manual harvest, never on a schedule, so their freshness is the date of the last manual read.
source_title: LGBS tax sales site; RealAuction Texas sites

statement: On LGBS and RealAuction listings the CAD account number identifies the parcel. The listing's tax-suit cause number can cover several parcels, so it is shown as a cause, never as a parcel number.
source_title: LGBS tax sales site; RealAuction Texas sites
evidence: harvesters/texas_harvester.py TexasSaleRow (cause_number -> parcel, account_number -> case_no); read-only SQL 2026-10-10: 32 LGBS causes on 2-26 active rows each

statement: East Baton Rouge Parish publishes its adjudicated-property list as open data under a Public Domain licence. The list's own last update is 2024-02-27, so it is shown as a dated list, never as current availability.
source_title: East Baton Rouge open data: Adjudicated Property

statement: Louisiana's statutes on adjudicated property and its sale have not been read and recorded here.
Michigan's tax foreclosure and auction statute (the General Property Tax Act) has not been read and recorded here. Each tracked county's own sale page is recorded below.

The Detroit Land Bank Authority and the Oceana County Land Bank publish their own inventories. Both are collected and await customer-publication review; customers do not see them until a review approves them.
source_title: Detroit Land Bank Authority inventory (ArcGIS item); Oceana County Land Bank page

statement: Albany County's tax sale sells a tax lien certificate on each listed parcel, not the land. No certificate exists before the sale.
source_title: Albany County 2026 tax sale properties, 1st list (ArcGIS item)
evidence: docs/six-state-expansion.md (WY row: 'the sale sells certificates; none exist before the sale')

statement: Wyoming's tax sale and redemption statutes have not been read and recorded here.

The Georgetown County Forfeited Land Commission's own pages state that properties from the most recent tax sale are still in the redemption period. This app treats a land row as available only after its sale is past a twelve-month redemption period.
South Carolina's twelve-month redemption period is cited here (S.C. Code 12-51-90) but the section's text has not been read and recorded.
Forfeited Land Commission property is offered 'AS IS, WHERE IS'; the transferring deed is a quit claim deed, and the Commission decides a bidder application and then states the total amount due.
source_title: Georgetown County Forfeited Land Commission program page

statement: Douglas County's annual tax lien sale sells a lien on each advertised account, not the land. The Treasurer states the 2026 internet tax lien sale is held November 5, 2026.
source_title: Douglas County Tax Sale List Locations (open data item; Treasurer's sale notice)

statement: Colorado's tax lien sale, redemption and treasurer's deed statutes have not been read and recorded here.
Wisconsin counties sell tax-deeded land by bid (Wis. Stat. 75.35 / 75.69 are cited from a search, not read).
The St. Louis Land Reutilization Authority's inventory publishes no price and no application process; the LRA's process has not been captured.
source_title: City of St. Louis open data: LRA inventory

statement: Missouri's land reutilization statutes have not been read and recorded here.

Oklahoma County's list states: 'Once the County owns these properties, they can be purchased by the public through a bidding process.' Bids go on the Treasurer's bid form; the list's 'Suggested Initial Bid Amount' is a suggestion, not a stated minimum or price.
source_title: Oklahoma County Treasurer - County Owned Property

statement: Oklahoma's tax resale statutes have not been read and recorded here.
Fayette County Tax Claim Bureau repository properties are sold by sealed bid; rows the list marks 'Bid Received' are pending. The list is dated by its own document name (Repository Update 10-7-2025).
source_title: Fayette County Tax Claim Bureau - Repository Update 10-7-2025

statement: Pennsylvania's Real Estate Tax Sale Law provisions on repository sales (including the taxing bodies' consent) have not been read and recorded here.
Ramsey County's tax-forfeited land layer marks parcels 'Available for purchase'; only those are shown. The layer publishes a minimum bid and no purchase link.
source_title: Ramsey County Tax Forfeited Land (public layer)

statement: Minnesota's tax-forfeited land statutes have not been read and recorded here.

The Shelby County Land Bank's own portal lists county-owned parcels already taken through delinquent-tax sales ('County DTP'). A parcel is offered only when the portal shows status 'FOR SALE' and available 'Y'. There is no auction or sale date on this source.
source_title: Shelby County Land Bank - ePropertyPlus portal

statement: The Land Bank links an 'Offer to Purchase and Sales Agreement Packet'. It is a scanned PDF with no text layer, so its terms have not been read.

Tennessee's delinquent tax sale and redemption statutes have not been read and recorded here; the conclusion that Tennessee sells no tax-lien certificates comes from a survey (docs/tennessee-survey.md), not a statute read.
